I'm amazed that candidates for President propose schemes like this. As President Paul would have less power than he currently does to introduce or vote on measures leading up to this. He knows better too. As someone who is reportedly running to reign in government's overreach, he could start by educating Americans about the proper role of the Presidency as it is outlined in the Constitution.

As a technical legal matter. Very little. It'd require a change to the law and that's entirely in the hands of the congress, specifically the house since it'd be an appropriations bill.

But as a practical political matter a president has enormous power far beyond any individual legislator to push his agenda in congress. Members of his party, including the leadership in congress look to him to set their collective agenda. He's the only one who has been elected by the entire nation and the only one that can claim to have a national mandate. He's the only one that can truly dominate the news if he chooses to. It's extremely difficult for the leaders in his own party to oppose him in any significant way and very hard for the opposition to not at least sit down with him and offer some kind of compromise.

Look at the government shutdowns during the Clinton administration and more recently under Obama. Congress passed the appropriations bills required to fund the government but they cut funding for programs the President wanted so rather than lose the programs he pushed for he shut down the entire government. Did the president get blamed for the shutdown? They were equally at fault, arguably the president is more at fault since they did their job and passed an appropriations bill and they're the legislators while he's the executive that's supposed to execute whatever laws they pass.

But that's not how it worked out. Congress got the blame and ultimately backed both times because the president has the ear of the people in a way that congress doesn't. Even people who agreed with congresses goals blamed them for the resulting impasse.

I'm amazed at how many Americans think the president decides everything. Of course presidential candidates take full advantage of it. Just vote for me and I'll do this and that. Things a president can't do.
